column1: What does topology keep and what does it ignore?
column2: It keeps connectedness and holes. It ignores length, angle and area: stretching and bending are allowed, cutting and gluing are not.
\( \chi = V - E + F \). Any ball-shaped polyhedron gives 2. A one-hole (torus) polyhedron gives 0.

column1: What is a homotopy between two loops?
column2: A continuous deformation of one loop into the other, a movie with no cuts.
\( \mathbb{Z} \). A loop is classified by its winding number.

column1: \( \pi_1 \) of the sphere and of the torus?
column2: Sphere: trivial (every loop shrinks). Torus: \( \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z} \) (laps around the tube and around the hole).

column1: What do the Betti numbers \( b_0, b_1, b_2 \) count?
column2: Connected pieces, independent loops that bound nothing, and enclosed voids.

column1: Key identity of the boundary map?
column2: \( \partial \circ \partial = 0 \): the boundary of a boundary is zero.

Every continuous tangent vector field on a sphere is zero somewhere. A torus can be combed flat.
The indices of the zeros of a tangent vector field add up to \( \chi \).

column1: What does a persistence barcode show?
column2: For each hole, the range of scales \( \varepsilon \) over which it exists. Long bars are real structure, short bars are noise.
